Empirical Research Plan – ADA and Employment of the Disabled

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) complemented by an event-study specification.

Justification
• The ADA is a nationwide policy that takes effect at a well-defined date, so the “before/after” dimension is time.  
• Treatment varies across individuals: those with a work-limiting disability (treated) vs. those without (control).  
• CPS provides repeated cross-sections at monthly frequency, permitting pre-trend tests and dynamic effects.  
• Because implementation was staggered (Title I became binding for firms ≥25 workers in July 1992 and for 15–24 workers in July 1994) we can run a robustness DDD that contrasts large-firm vs. small-firm labor markets (using industry-size proxies) or exploit state pre-ADA disability laws.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment Variable  
  treat_i = 1 if the respondent self-reports a work-limiting disability (CPS variable: “disability” or the work-limitation supplement).

Control Group  
  treat_i = 0 (non-disabled individuals aged 18–64).

Treatment Timing / Event Date  
  post_t = 1 for observations on/after July 1992 (main), 0 before.  
  We will also estimate an event-study with month dummies 1988–1996 to visualise dynamics and test parallel trends.

Alternative / Robustness Treatment Definition  
  • Post 1994 dummy (when coverage expanded to 15–24 employee firms).  
  • State×year variation in pre-existing disability discrimination statutes (triple-diff).

No RDD running variable is required.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Parallel Trends: In the absence of the ADA, employment outcomes for disabled and non-disabled individuals would have followed parallel trajectories.  
Plausibility: Reasonable but not guaranteed. We can test with pre-1990 event-study coefficients.

A2. No Differential Anticipation: Firms/workers did not meaningfully adjust prior to July 1992 in ways that differentially affect the disabled.  
Plausibility: Medium. The ADA was signed in 1990, leaving two years for anticipation. We can include a “pseudo-post” (1990–1991) indicator to detect anticipatory effects.

A3. Stable Composition: The definition and self-reporting of disability remain consistent.  
Plausibility: Some risk—CPS redesigned disability questions in 1994. We will run robustness dropping 1994 redesign months and controlling for observable health proxies.

A4. No Spillovers: ADA should not directly affect employment of the non-disabled (control).  
Plausibility: Some spillovers are possible (firms substitute away from the disabled). That biases us toward finding negative effects; we will acknowledge in interpretation.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Main Threats & Mitigation
────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Divergent Pre-Trends  
   • Mitigation: event-study graph; placebo DID using pre-1988 vs. 1988–1990.

T2. Measurement Change in CPS (1994 redesign)  
   • Mitigation: include survey redesign dummy; robustness dropping 1994–95; compare trends in rotations not affected.

T3. Macro Shocks / Recession of early 1990s hitting disabled differently  
   • Mitigation: add state×year unemployment rate controls, industry×year fixed effects, and run DDD using states with pre-existing disability laws (if law already in place, ADA’s marginal effect should be muted).

────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # high-performance fixed-effects DID
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data Loading
cps <- fread("cps_1988_1996.csv")  # assume monthly CPS extract

# 2. Variable Construction
cps[, year  := year(date)]
cps[, month := month(date)]

# Work-limiting disability dummy (assuming variable 'disab')
cps[, treat := as.integer(disab == 1)]

# Post dummy: July 1992 or later
cps[, post  := as.integer(date >= as.IDate("1992-07-01"))]

# Employment outcome (employment status == employed)
cps[, employed := as.integer(empstat == "Employed")]

# Control variables
cps[, `:=`(age2 = age^2,
           female = as.integer(sex == "Female"))]

# 3. Main DID Specification
did_main <- feols(employed ~ treat*post + age + age2 + female + educ +
                  i(state, year) | state + year_month,
                  data = cps, cluster = ~state)

summary(did_main)

# 4. Event Study
cps[, rel_time := as.integer((year - 1992)*12 + (month - 7))]
cps[, rel_time_cat := fifelse(rel_time < -36, -36,
                       fifelse(rel_time > 48, 48, rel_time))]

event <- feols(employed ~ i(rel_time_cat, treat, ref = -1) + age + age2 +
               female + educ | state + year_month,
               data = cps, cluster = ~state)

iplot(event, ref.line = 0, xlab = "Months relative to July 1992",
      main = "Event-study: ADA and Employment of Disabled")

# 5. Robustness: Drop 1994 redesign months
robust <- feols(employed ~ treat*post + age + age2 + female + educ +
                i(state, year) | state + year_month,
                data = cps[year < 1994 | year > 1995],
                cluster = ~state)
summary(robust)
```

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────
Prior based on economic theory mixed:  
• Compliance costs and firing costs could reduce hiring of the disabled ⇒ negative employment effect.  
• Anti-discrimination could increase retention/hiring ⇒ positive effect.  

Empirically, most studies find a modest decline. I expect a −2 to −4 pp change in the employment rate of the disabled relative to the non-disabled during 1992–1996.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
(C1-C5 loosely follow Angrist & Pischke, Roth 2023)

C1. Pre-Treatment Parallel Trends demonstrated? … 0.8  
C2. Correct treatment timing / no anticipation? … 0.6  
C3. No simultaneous policies confounding? … 0.5  
C4. No compositional changes in groups? … 0.6  
C5. Correct inference & clustering? … 1.0  

Overall average ≈ 0.7 → reasonably credible but not bullet-proof.
